title_zh: 清算比特币储备公司的那个人
subtitle_zh: Woodmont Partners 执行成员 Tice Brown 做客 Money Stuff：他给 Matt Levine 发了一封邮件，说自己想清算一家比特币储备公司（Empery Digital）——而这封邮件后来成了诉讼证据。两人从 DAT（数字资产储备公司）PIPE 的兴衰聊起，谈到 MNAV 与 PB 口径下折价/溢价的镜像交易、非交叉抵押杠杆的诱惑；再拐进他更古怪的生意：用量化方法买卖艺术品和恐龙化石、六只零现金流房地产债券的 defeasance（债务解除）、1031 置换加“先还本再放款”抵押的税务魔术、MS-13 占领的租约物业、阿肯色州小镇银行的放贷文化，以及保险浮存金、内布拉斯加与Mark Walter、Todd Boehly 的资本模式；最后是 SpaceX 与特斯拉合并、EA 债券 defeasance 官司，还有 Matt 在金融危机后的高盛“什么都没做的六个月”。

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios. Podcasts.
turns.zh: 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）。播客。

turns.en: Radio. News. Hello and welcome to the Money Stuff Podcast. I'm Matt Levine. I wrote the Money Stuff column for Bloomberg Opinion. We have a guest today, Tice Brown. Why don't you say what your deal is?
turns.zh: 广播。新闻。大家好，欢迎来到《Money Stuff》播客。我是 Matt Levine，为彭博观点（Bloomberg Opinion）撰写 Money Stuff 专栏。今天我们请来了一位嘉宾，Tice Brown。你来说说你自己是干什么的吧？

turns.en: My name's Tyce Brown. I'm the managing member of a group of single-member LLCs that we call, in collection, Woodmont Partners.
turns.zh: 我叫 Tice Brown。我是一批单一成员有限责任公司（single-member LLC）的执行成员（managing member），这些公司合在一起，我们统称为 Woodmont Partners。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: But it's a family office. I'm just a guy. And your title, Money Stuff, actually gives me a huge amount of cover. Because all the time, like, my wife's parents, who are, like, well-credentialed and coastal, say, what does Tyce do? Oh, yeah, he does investing stuff. And, like, people get that. You don't have to invest in stuff. I do things that drive my curiosity, and we try to make money. I didn't come from money. My dad's a community college teacher in Arkansas, and my mom's a county doctor. I've tried to access leverage in intelligent ways, and we have a grab bag of a lot of weird assets that I can talk about.
turns.zh: 但它其实就是一家家族办公室（family office）。我就是一个人。而且你这个栏目标题——Money Stuff（钱的那些事儿）——其实给了我极大的掩护。因为我太太的父母，那种学历光鲜、住在东西海岸的人，总是问：Tice 是干什么的？哦，对，他是搞投资那类事儿的。大家一听就懂了。你不必真去投资什么具体的东西。我做的是那些能勾起我好奇心的事，然后我们试着赚钱。我不是含着金汤匙出生的。我爸在阿肯色州一所社区学院教书，我妈是县里的医生。我一直试图用聪明的方式去撬动杠杆，我们手上有一大堆稀奇古怪的资产，我可以慢慢讲。

turns.en: I would like that. You send me really good emails. I sometimes do talks, and people are like, what are your ideas? I sometimes get good emails from people, and I try to describe the characteristics of a good email, and I got an email from Tice in February that is now on the record in the court case saying, I'd like to liquidate a Bitcoin treasury company. I'd like to speak publicly about it. And it's one of those things where like, I'm just going along my day and that email comes in and I'm like, why have I never thought about liquidating a Bitcoin treasury company? But you had. Tell me about it.
turns.zh: 我很乐意听。你给我发的邮件真的很好。我有时去做演讲，别人会问：你的想法都是从哪儿来的？我时不时会收到一些好邮件，我还试着总结过什么样的邮件才算好邮件。今年二月我收到 Tice 的一封邮件，那封信现在已经作为证据出现在官司卷宗里了——信上写的是：我想清算一家比特币储备公司（Bitcoin treasury company），而且我想公开谈这件事。当时我正过着我普通的一天，这封邮件蹦出来，我心想：我怎么从来没想到要去清算一家比特币储备公司？可你想到了。说说吧。

turns.en: So there was... A long period of time, months, you know, six, eight, 12 months when there was a fad in the U.S. capital markets to raise cash through a pipe in small public clean shells, usually on the NASDAQ and the New York Stock Exchange, although not exclusively. And you'd raise like $ 500 billion and a lot of them would trade at a significant premium to crypto they bought. We can use Bitcoin as an example. These guys would raise $ 500 million, buy $ 500 million of Bitcoin, and it would trade for a huge premium, say a billion. And they could issue more shares, buy more crypto, and go to infinity, free money. And the most famous one was MicroStrategy.
turns.zh: 事情是这样的……有相当长一段时间——六个月、八个月、十二个月吧——美国资本市场上流行过一阵风潮：通过 PIPE（私募股权投资已上市公司股份）在规模很小、账目干净的上市壳公司里融资，通常是在纳斯达克或者纽交所，但也不限于这两家。你会募到大约五亿美元，然后这些公司里有很多，交易价格会大幅高于它们买入的加密货币。拿比特币举例：这些人募五亿美元、买五亿美元的比特币，然后股价却按十亿美元的市值交易。于是他们可以增发股票、买更多加密货币，如此循环到无穷大——白来的钱。其中最出名的一家是 MicroStrategy（微策略）。

turns.en: We've talked a lot about MicroStrategy.
turns.zh: MicroStrategy 我们已经聊过很多次了。

turns.en: It's just an infinite money machine.
turns.zh: 它就是一台无限印钞机。

turns.en: Without a pipe. Well, I mean, whatever.
turns.zh: 而且没用 PIPE。嗯，我是说，随便吧。

turns.en: They had an ATM.
turns.zh: 他们有 ATM 增发（at-the-market，市价增发计划）。

turns.en: Yeah. Right.
turns.zh: 对，没错。

turns.en: Imprey did a pipe. I participated in the pipe. Right.
turns.zh: Empery 做了 PIPE。我参与了那次 PIPE。对。

turns.en: So I was going to say, like, strategy is like, there's a weird guy around a public company and he's like, I'm going to start putting our cash into Bitcoin.
turns.zh: 我刚想说，Strategy（也就是 MicroStrategy）的情况是这样的：一家上市公司旁边有个怪人，他说，我要开始把我们的现金拿去买比特币了。

turns.en: But there were dozens of copycat pipes.
turns.zh: 但后来出现了几十个照猫画虎的 PIPE。

turns.en: But yeah, the pipes, like, that's an interesting reason. So a pipe is like, you have a promoter, you have a small kind of cleanish shell public company, and you have a set of target investors who will invest privately in transforming the shell into Into a Bitcoin treasury company, or they call it a DAT now, a digital asset treasury company. Exactly. And you're one of those investors. Like, who are these investors? Like, how do they find, because I assume at that time, like you could round up $ 500 million for a DAT pipe in like a week.
turns.zh: 但没错，这些 PIPE 本身就是个有意思的点。所谓 PIPE，就是：你有一个推销者（promoter），有一家规模不大、还算干净的上市壳公司，还有一批目标投资人，他们会私下出资，把这个壳公司改造成一家比特币储备公司——现在他们管这个叫 DAT，也就是数字资产储备公司（digital asset treasury company）。——正是。而你就是这样一位投资人。那这些投资人都是谁？他们是怎么被找到的？因为在我看来，那阵子你要为一笔 DAT 的 PIPE 凑齐五亿美元，大概一个星期就够了。

turns.en: I'm an intellectually curious guy. We have a lot of capital looking for weird stuff to do.
turns.zh: 我是个求知欲很强的人。我们手上有大量资本，在到处找古怪的事情做。

turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: The idea of investing in a shell and having a trade at a premium, which maybe we did. for a band that was really interesting to me. And we wrote a couple million dollar check to see if that was a phenomenon that would continue. In this case, it didn't.
turns.zh: 投资一个壳公司、然后在溢价里做交易——这个想法，也许我们真这么干过——在那个我看来很有意思的价格区间里。我们开出了几百万美元的支票，去看看这现象会不会延续下去。在这个案例里，它没有延续。

turns.en: Is it a lot of like crypto focused hedge funds?
turns.zh: 投这些的多是专注加密货币的对冲基金吗？

turns.en: No, no, no. If you look at the list of the people that invest in the pipes, it's like major hedge funds, top 10 pod shops, like each will write a $ 2 million, $ 5 million check to a bunch of these guys. And they're I mean, I think seen as intelligent investors and they were doing a bunch of these.
turns.zh: 不不不。如果你去看参与这些 PIPE 的投资人名单，那都是主流对冲基金、前十大的多组平台（pod shop）——每家都会给一堆这样的项目开两百万、五百万美元的支票。而且他们……我是说，我认为他们被视为聪明的投资人，而他们做了一大堆这种交易。

turns.en: Were they hedged? Like were they?
turns.zh: 他们做了对冲吗？就是说，有没有？

turns.en: I don't talk to him. I'm one guy sitting at home alone and I'm looking for weird stuff to do.
turns.zh: 我不跟他们打交道。我就是一个人独自坐在家里，找些古怪的事情做。

turns.en: Were you hedged?
turns.zh: 那你对冲了吗？

turns.en: At which point, right? So I've owned this for a year and a half. And like this changed over time.
turns.zh: 在哪个时点对冲，对吧？我持有这东西已经一年半了，而这个情况是随时间变化的。

turns.en: By hedged, I mean. Short Bitcoin. These are things that for a while. The trade was that they traded at 100% premium to their net asset value. So you could capture that premium by buying the DAT shares at $ 100 and selling $ 50 worth of Bitcoin. And then you weren't levered to Bitcoin prices. You just had the premium.
turns.zh: 我说的对冲，意思是做空比特币。这类股票有一阵子的交易逻辑是这样的：它们相对净资产值（NAV）有 100% 的溢价。所以你可以用 100 美元买入 DAT 的股票，同时卖出价值 50 美元的比特币，来捕获这个溢价。这样你就不承担比特币价格的杠杆敞口了，你手里只剩那个溢价。

turns.en: There's a more important word that you haven't said yet, which is MNAV. Do you know what MNAV is?
turns.zh: 还有一个更重要的词你还没说出来，就是 MNAV。你知道 MNAV 是什么吗？

turns.en: MNAV is, okay. Why don't you explain what MNAV is? Because you've explained it.
turns.zh: MNAV 是……好吧，那你来解释一下 MNAV 是什么吧，反正你已经解释过一遍了。

turns.en: So it's the assets in crypto compared to the enterprise value, total enterprise value of a public company. Which leads to some really wonky math. And I think it was invented by strategy to show off how many Bitcoin they had, because they have an extraordinarily convoluted capital structure.
turns.zh: 就是加密货币资产与一家上市公司的企业价值（enterprise value）、总企业价值之比。这会导出一些非常古怪的算术。我记得这个指标是 Strategy 发明的，用来炫耀自己有多少比特币，因为他们的资本结构极其复杂纠结。

turns.en: Yeah, they have everything.
turns.zh: 是啊，他们什么都有。

turns.en: And they've got a complex structure. So if you're comparing, can I give an illustrative example? Imagine two companies that each have, for super simple math, a billion dollars of Bitcoin at T1. A billion, a billion. And imagine one of them is totally equity funded. It has no debt. And it's It trades at 96% MNAV. People love that. This is what percent MNAV. It trades at 0.96 MNAV. So it trades for $ 960 million, a billion dollars of Bitcoin. Not a huge discount. You could imagine, there's a hypothetical, but you could imagine a company with a billion dollars of Bitcoin and $ 900 million of margin or other debt, fixed obligations, that also traded at 96% of MNAV. what does its market cap on a PB basis, price to book basis, look like?
turns.zh: 而且他们的结构很复杂。所以如果你要做比较的话——我能举个说明性的例子吗？想象有两家公司，为了算术极简，在 T1 时点各自持有十亿美元的比特币。十亿，十亿。假设其中一家完全由股权融资，没有任何负债，它的交易价格是 MNAV 的 96%。大家很喜欢这个说法：这是百分之多少 MNAV。它以 0.96 倍 MNAV 交易，也就是说十亿美元的比特币，市值九亿六千万美元。折价不算大。你可以想象——这是个假设，但你可以想象——另一家公司同样有十亿美元的比特币，但还有九亿美元的保证金借款或者其他债务、固定偿付义务，而它也按 MNAV 的 96% 交易。那么以市净率（PB，price-to-book）口径看，它的市值会是什么样？

turns.en: Is MNAV.
turns.zh: 那 MNAV 呢？

turns.en: On the EV? So if it had $ 900 million of US dollar debt.
turns.zh: 是按企业价值（EV）算的。所以如果它有九亿美元的美元债务——

turns.en: So it's really at 96% of.
turns.zh: 所以它其实是在（企业价值的）96%。

turns.en: We're getting to the AMV.
turns.zh: 我们正要说到 MNAV 这一块。

turns.en: So it's like at a 40% discount on equity, right?
turns.zh: 所以在股权层面它相当于折价 40%，对吧？

turns.en: On a PB basis, it'd be at 60%, right? And so that's just an illustrative example that played into the Ampreet situation over the year because they used debt-funded buybacks, which was not super crazy, depending on what you thought would happen to the price of Bitcoin, right? So it's hedged at first when Bitcoin was at $ 117, 000. We had to disclose all our trading and all the subsequent lawsuits and 13D and everything. So we had some short. And as the price of Bitcoin went down, we removed the short. We bought more stock. You could imagine it as a way to get a significant amount of non-cross-collateralized leverage of the price of Bitcoin. Do you see? Yeah. How if you think... that billion dollars of Bitcoin is at $ 70, 000 of Bitcoin, and you believe it will return to $ 117, 000. Buying that at 96% MNV even might be really, really attractive because you're buying it 60% of PV. That's not the fun bit. The fun bit is if Bitcoin goes from $ 70, 000 Bitcoin to $ 117, 000 Bitcoin, your $ 960 million of fixed obligation stays flat, and your book value multiplies, and that You know, silly example is what occurred here or what I was.
turns.zh: 按 PB 口径算，它是 60%，对吧？这只是一个说明性的例子，但在这一年里它恰好套进了 Empery 的情况，因为他们用了债务融资的回购——这不算特别疯狂，取决于你怎么看比特币价格未来的走势。对吧？所以一开始是对冲过的：比特币在 117,000 美元的时候，我们必须披露所有交易，以及后续所有的诉讼、13D 表格等等。所以我们持有一些空头。随着比特币价格下跌，我们平掉了空头，买了更多股票。你可以把它理解成一种手段，去获得大量非交叉抵押（non-cross-collateralized）的比特币价格杠杆。你明白吗？——明白。——如果你觉得……那十亿美元的比特币现在只值七万美元一枚，而你相信它会回到 117,000 美元，那么即便按 96% 的 MNAV 买入也可能非常、非常有吸引力，因为你其实是以 PB 的 60% 在买。而这还不是好玩的部分。好玩的部分是：如果比特币从七万美元涨回 117,000 美元，你那九亿六千万美元的固定偿付义务一动不动，而你的账面价值会成倍增长。就是这么个傻例子，而这正是这里发生的事——或者说，是我当时……

turns.en: Hoping to occur here. So then you eventually wanted to liquidate it. So like.
turns.zh: ……希望它发生的事。那么后来你最终想要清算它。所以说……

turns.en: That was after awkward conflict with management. I was originally a 13G slyler.
turns.zh: 那是在跟管理层发生了尴尬的冲突之后。我最初是一个 13G 表格的申报人（filer）。

turns.en: Because like when I wrote about this after getting your email, I was like, there's a trade that was in huge vogue, which is you can take $ 100 worth of Bitcoin and sell it for $ 200 in the stock exchange. And now that trade has flipped.
turns.zh: 因为当我收到你的邮件、然后写了这件事之后，我的感觉是：曾经有一笔极其风靡的交易，就是你可以把价值 100 美元的比特币在股票市场上按 200 美元卖掉。而现在这笔交易反转了。

turns.en: Five months later. So now we're past wearing a head. You've gone from August 2025. to January, 2026, when all of these went from 200% MNAV to, in this case, I can't remember, it's like in the 70s on an MNAV basis, but on this PB, let's go back to that, it got down to 57% PB. And I think Bitcoin is an interesting gambling proxy. Like the intrinsic value is based on the discounted cash flows that you'll receive in the future from Asda. But we do a good business in art. We do a good business in a bunch of non-cash flowing real estate, I think there's a human desire, clearly, to seek gambling. And I think Bitcoin has been a gambling proxy that's been out-competed by Cal Street and PolyMarket and a bunch of other things. But I think it's an interesting gambling proxy that might return. And if you can get this non-recourse leverage on it, non-cross-collateralized leverage on it, you could achieve extraordinary outcomes if Bitcoin returned to even where it had been before, much less a higher number.
turns.zh: 五个月之后。所以我们现在已经过了要戴对冲（hedge）的阶段。时间从 2025 年 8 月走到 2026 年 1 月，所有这些公司的 MNAV 从 200% 掉到了——这一家我记不清了，大概是 70% 出头——但如果按我们刚才说的 PB 口径，它跌到了 57% 的 PB。我认为比特币是个有意思的赌博替代品（gambling proxy）。所谓内在价值，是基于你未来能收到的折现现金流。但我们在艺术品上生意做得不错，在一堆不产生现金流的房地产上生意也做得不错。我认为人类显然有一种寻求赌博的欲望，而比特币一直是一个赌博替代品，只不过现在被 Kalshi、Polymarket 之类的一堆东西抢走了生意。但我认为它是个有意思的赌博替代品，可能会卷土重来。而如果你能拿到这种无追索权（non-recourse）、非交叉抵押的杠杆，那么即使比特币只是回到它此前的位置、更不用说到更高的数字，你都能获得异乎寻常的回报。

turns.en: So when I got an email from you being like, I want to liquidate it, I was like, oh, of course. If it's trading at a discount, it's just the same trade in reverse. You buy shares for 80 cents and you liquidate the Bitcoin for 100 cents. Of course. But you were still like, I mean, by the time you emailed me, you changed your mind. But for a long time, you're like, this discount is great because it's a way for me to have like a very levered upside bet on Bitcoin gambling.
turns.zh: 所以当我收到你的邮件、你说‘我想清算它’的时候，我心想：哦，当然了。如果它按折价交易，那就是同一笔交易反过来做。你用 80 美分买入股票，然后把比特币按 100 美分清算掉。当然。但你当时还是……我是说，到你给我发邮件的时候，你已经改主意了。但在很长一段时间里，你的想法是：这个折价太棒了，因为它让我能对‘比特币赌博’持有一笔高杠杆的上行押注。

turns.en: It wasn't a long time. I mean, a lot of the money was deployed in a short period of time. There was a day when the stock was down 23%, the trading price of stock. So if you have something that was already trading at some discount and the stock falls 20 plus percent a day that's a day you're gonna buy a bunch and i did and so then you run into the securities law obligation of i sit down with security attorney and talk through my conversations i've had with management or anybody and we follow 13g and then i asked the management to get a cheeseburger and it's been messy yeah it was messy after that named in some lawsuits yeah that was the name i was asked to be a witness and And some lawsuits. And my name was in the lawsuits. That doesn't mean you're named in the lawsuits.
turns.zh: 其实没那么长。很多钱是在很短的时间内投出去的。有一天股价跌了 23%，就是交易价格。所以如果你手上有个东西本来就打了折，而股价一天再跌 20% 以上，那正是你该大买特买的一天——我就买了。然后你就撞上了证券法的义务：我会坐下来跟证券律师一条条过，把我跟管理层或者任何人的沟通都梳理一遍，我们按 13G 来走。然后我约管理层出来吃了个芝士汉堡（意即摊牌），从此就一团糟了。——是啊，那之后确实一团糟。——在一些诉讼里被点了名。——是啊，那个名字，我被要求做证人，还出现在一些诉讼里。我的名字出现在了诉讼文件里。——这并不意味着你被列为了当事人。

turns.en: I felt named. I'm sorry. Yeah. Like one problem with the dad trade is that it was the Vogue trade of like, you know, a year and a half ago. Sure. And now there's a new Vogue trade, which is pivoting to AI. And they have done that. Have they? Well, they've announced that.
turns.zh: 我感觉自己是被点名了。抱歉。——是啊。DAT 这笔交易的一个问题在于：它是一年半以前最风靡的那笔交易。当然。而现在有了新的风靡交易，就是转向 AI。——他们真这么做了吗？——他们宣布了这个意向。

turns.en: They've announced intent to. I don't have any further information about.
turns.zh: 他们只是宣布了意向。这方面我没有更多信息了。

turns.en: Are they like less? correlated to Bitcoin now? Yes.
turns.zh: 那他们现在跟比特币的相关性是不是更低了？——是的。

turns.en: My understanding is they have, I mean, just relying on the public disclosures, quite a bit of cash, and a contracted agreement to invest in a data center, and they have an electrical investment they've already made, and still some Bitcoin, but much less correlated than they were. But I wanted correlation to Bitcoin at a certain discount. And I wanted the leverage they had at a certain amount. And honestly, we have a bunch of different investments. And the more dislocated they get, the more you allocate to that. And we allocated a good bit to this because it was interesting dislocated. And for a while, they were buying back a lot of stock.
turns.zh: 我的理解是——我只依赖公开披露——他们手上有相当多的现金，有一份投资数据中心的合同安排，还有一笔已经投下去的电力相关投资，另外还有一些比特币，但相关性比之前低多了。而我想要的，是在某个折价水平上拿到对比特币的相关性，以及我想要他们那个规模的杠杆。老实说，我们有一堆不同的投资，越是出现错配（dislocation），我们就越往那边加码。我们在这一家上加了不少，因为它的错配很有意思。而且有一阵子他们在大量回购股票。

turns.en: Like at some point you were like, they should be buying back all the stock and closing the discount.
turns.zh: 有一阵子你的想法是：他们应该把所有股票都回购掉，把这个折价消灭掉。

turns.en: They did a bunch of buybacks. They did a bunch of buybacks. But why does closing the discount matter to you?
turns.zh: 他们确实做了不少回购。——他们确实做了不少回购。但消灭折价这件事，对你来说为什么重要？

turns.en: I guess it doesn't. It matters to me if I think about like the entry at the trade being, which it wasn't for you. But if you think about the entry being like you see a debt trading at a discount, you're like, I'm going to buy it at a discount, hedge the Bitcoin and just try to capture that spread. But you're like, that's small potatoes for you.
turns.zh: 我想其实也不重要。对我来说它重要，是如果我把这笔交易的入场逻辑想成……而对你来说并不是这样。但如果你把入场逻辑想成：你看到一只 DAT 按折价交易，你说，我要按折价买进来，把比特币对冲掉，就赚这个价差。但对你来说，那是小钱。

turns.en: Imagine if something traded at 57% of just cash. Forget the Bitcoin debt, but imagine something was trading. And you were able to buy in, and they did successfully for a while, half a percent of shares outstanding a day. You're increasing now by 25 bips a day or something, 20 bips a day. Like there's 250.
turns.zh: 想象有个东西只按现金的 57% 交易——把比特币和债务都忘掉，就想象有个东西在这么交易。而且你还能买得进去，他们有一阵子确实成功地每天回购掉流通股的半个百分点。那你现在等于每天增厚 25 个基点，或者 20 个基点。一年有 250 个……

turns.en: Trading days in a year. 1.0025 raised to the 250th is like a huge return. I'm not a math guy, but NAV would go up a lot. Yeah, right. So it is the reverse of the classic micro-strategy.
turns.zh: ……交易日。1.0025 的 250 次方，那是个巨大的回报。我不是搞数学的，但 NAV 会涨很多。——是啊，没错。所以这正好是经典 MicroStrategy 玩法的反面。

turns.en: It's exactly.
turns.zh: 完全就是。

turns.en: They called it accretive dilution, where they would sell stock at a premium, and that would increase the NAV. And then here it's like they're buying stock at a discount, so it increases the NAV.
turns.zh: 他们管那叫‘增厚式稀释’（accretive dilution）：按溢价卖出股票，从而提高每股 NAV。而这里正好相反：他们按折价买入股票，所以也提高了 NAV。

turns.en: I mean, micro-strategy is trading at a premium to MNEV again.
turns.zh: 我是说，MicroStrategy 现在又重新按 MNAV 溢价交易了。

turns.en: A bunch of them are.
turns.zh: 有一大批都是。

turns.en: Yeah, I guess. I don't know. This is the only one I've been in.
turns.zh: 嗯，大概是吧。我不清楚。这是我唯一投过的一家。

turns.en: Is it the only one you were in the pipe for?
turns.zh: 这是你唯一参与过 PIPE 的一家吗？

turns.en: It's the only pipe I've been in. We had some other exposures, some other ones, but nothing significant.
turns.zh: 这是我唯一参与过的 PIPE。我们在别家也有一些敞口，但都不重要。

turns.en: Who calls you about the dot pipes?
turns.zh: 谁会打电话给你谈这些 DAT 的 PIPE？

turns.en: It was on the lawsuit. I spent all day talking to people, right? I spent all day talking. Have you read Ari Emanuel's book yet? No. Roll the calls. That's all I do. I just call, call, call. I go through my battery of my phone two or three times a day and I find places to walk. I walk around Tompkins Square Park or I sit in my home and I talk on the phone all day. And we do, I don't know, 20 investments a year or something. We just talk all the time. I'm taking a call. Before I walked in here from a piece of art we're.
turns.zh: 是官司上认识的。我一整天都在跟人打电话，对吧？我一整天都在说话。你读过 Ari Emanuel 的书了吗？——没有。——把电话一轮轮打下去。我干的就是这个。我一直在打打打，手机电池一天要充两三次，然后我就找地方走路。我在汤普金斯广场公园（Tompkins Square Park）附近溜达，或者就坐在家里，一整天都在打电话。我们一年大概做二十笔投资吧。我们就是一直在聊。我走进来之前还接了一个电话，是关于一件艺术品，我们正在……

turns.en: Working on buying.
turns.zh: ……张罗着买下来。

turns.en: So it's fun.
turns.zh: 所以挺好玩的。

turns.en: You do art as an investment?
turns.zh: 你把艺术品当投资来做？

turns.en: I have an art dealership.
turns.zh: 我有一家艺术品经销行（art dealership）。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯，嗯。

turns.en: We've got maybe Tempstion, our capital in fine arts.
turns.zh: 我们大概有百分之十的资本放在艺术品（fine arts）上。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Mostly impressionists, but we have a bunch of other stuff. We have some dinosaur fossils. and an old master on negotiating.
turns.zh: 主要是印象派，但也有一堆别的东西。我们有一些恐龙化石，还有一幅正在洽购的古大师（Old Master）作品。

turns.en: That's a good business these days, right? Like dinosaur fossils?
turns.zh: 这年头这是门好生意吧？我是说恐龙化石？

turns.en: I'm chasing the hype.
turns.zh: 我就是在追热点。

turns.en: Oh, okay. So you like read the Bloomberg article about dinosaur fossils?
turns.zh: 哦，好吧。所以你也是看了彭博那篇关于恐龙化石的报道？

turns.en: Sotheby's has an extraordinary paleontology or like fossils team. Let's go back further. So I accidentally stumbled into an auction at Christie's last year and a half and recognized that there was a lot of other activity happening, not just people waving paddles. And so I made friends with a bunch of the people within Christie's and within Sotheby's and tried to figure out the economics behind what was going on. And that's been a huge, that's a significant profit center for my business is buying and selling art in the last couple of years. The spread between bid and ask is very wide.
turns.zh: 苏富比（Sotheby's）有一支极其出色的古生物——或者说化石——团队。我们往回说一点。大概一年半以前，我误打误撞进了一场佳士得（Christie's）的拍卖会，然后意识到现场还有很多别的活动在进行，不只是有人在举牌。于是我跟佳士得和苏富比里面的一堆人交上了朋友，试着搞清楚这背后到底是怎么赚钱的。这已经成了……过去这几年，买卖艺术品是我这门生意里一个很大的、很重要的利润来源。买价和卖价之间的价差非常宽。

turns.en: I have written them. Not a very transparent market.
turns.zh: 我写过这些。那不是个很透明的市场。

turns.en: All of my stuff's at auction or post-auction or almost entirely. I don't think people actually do a whole lot of digging. We have bought and sold a seven-figure piece of art this year, bought in February and sold in October and made seven times the price or six times the price from significant pieces with significant artists, significant auction houses. It's a weird market, man.
turns.zh: 我的东西几乎全部来自拍卖会现场或者拍卖会之后。我觉得大家其实并没有做多少深挖。今年我们买入又卖出了一件七位数（美元）的艺术品——二月买进、十月卖出，赚了七倍，或者六倍的价格——都是重量级艺术家的重量级作品，走的重量级拍卖行。这真是个奇怪的市场，哥们儿。

turns.en: What is the one-sentence explanation for Did the market for that artist's art go up 600% or is it like people are weird?
turns.zh: 用一句话解释一下：是那位艺术家的作品市场整体涨了 600%，还是说只是人很奇怪？

turns.en: The bid-ask spread is really wide and there is simple quantitative exercises.
turns.zh: 买卖价差非常宽，而且这里有一些很简单的量化功课可做。

turns.en: What does bid-ask spread mean when you're buying and selling at like open options?
turns.zh: 当你是在公开拍卖里买进卖出的时候，‘买卖价差’到底指什么？

turns.en: An estate sale.
turns.zh: 遗产清仓拍卖（estate sale）。

turns.en: Okay, you buy it.
turns.zh: 好，你把它买下来。

turns.en: You can see that it's an estate sale. You can offer really, really low and see if it sells or not. And you don't get hit very often. And then you love them and hang them on the wall and you write them up. I've written up little paragraphs about each one. So my house is full of pretty pictures.
turns.zh: 你看得出这是一场遗产清仓。你可以出价出得非常、非常低，看看能不能成交。而且你也不会经常被打脸。然后你就喜欢上它们，把它们挂在墙上，给它们写点说明。每一件我都写了一小段文字。所以我家里挂满了漂亮的画。

turns.en: That's good.
turns.zh: 这挺好。

turns.en: I've got a Picasso in my daughter's room. There's a Piet Mondrian in the playroom. There's a T-Rex call over for my son's crib. It's fun.
turns.zh: 我女儿房间里挂着一幅毕加索（Picasso），游戏室里有一幅皮特·蒙德里安（Piet Mondrian），我儿子的婴儿床上方挂着一件霸王龙（T-Rex）化石。挺好玩的。

turns.en: And you write little, like, wall talkers?
turns.zh: 你还写那种小小的……展签（wall text）？

turns.en: Yeah, I've got big paragraphs describing the significance of them. I have the first dollars, the St. Joachimthal dollar. We have a bunch of crazy stuff. I've had Van Goghs and Renoirs and Degas.
turns.zh: 对，我写了大段的文字来描述它们的意义。我有最早的‘美元’——约阿希姆斯塔尔（Joachimsthal）银币。我们还有一堆疯狂的东西。我经手过梵高、雷诺阿和德加。

turns.en: We should be filming this in your apartment.
turns.zh: 我们这期节目应该去你公寓里录。

turns.en: Come down. My car's up front. Let's go. It's been fun.
turns.zh: 下来吧。我的车就停在门口。走，肯定很有意思。

turns.en: Anyway, sorry.
turns.zh: 总之，抱歉，扯远了。

turns.en: So the Bed-Ess road is very wide, and you can get a little bit of financing, not as much as I'd like. And you don't have to hold them in long as you'd think. And you can do quantitative analysis on the per square inch basis. It's just like real estate. And you can bid 20% of what you think it's worth.
turns.zh: 所以说买卖价差很宽，而且你能弄到一点融资——没有我想要的那么多。你也不需要像大家以为的那样持有那么久。你还可以按每平方英寸来做量化分析，就跟房地产一样。你可以直接出你心里估值的 20%。

turns.en: Is it like linear in square inches?
turns.zh: 这个跟平方英寸是线性关系吗？

turns.en: It's not a straight line. There's a curve to it because people don't like the smallest. Although there's been like little Raphael that sold for $ 50 million. And the big, big ones are really hard. I got this VR that was like six feet by six feet that was like really hard versus the value of it. So there's like a frown to the end of the line. But we just tried out what it should be worth. And you look at things of similar format, be it wall and canvas or paper and same arrow or same subject matter. And we do a little quantitative analysis, super simply, but really low. And we bought a bunch of fun stuff.
turns.zh: 不是一条直线，是有一条曲线的，因为大家不喜欢最小的那些。不过也有过小幅的拉斐尔（Raphael）卖出五千万美元的情况。而特别大幅的就很难。我有一件大概是六英尺乘六英尺的，相对于它的价值来说就非常难出手。所以这条线的末端是往下弯的，像个皱眉的形状。但我们就是去试它应该值多少钱。你会去看形制类似的作品——不管是布面油画还是纸本、同一个艺术家、或者同一类题材。我们做一点点非常简单的量化分析，出价出得非常低。然后我们就买了一堆好玩的东西。

turns.en: So you're running like a quant art fund. Okay. I like.
turns.zh: 所以你其实在运营一只量化艺术品基金。好。我喜欢。

turns.en: That's like 10% of the capital.
turns.zh: 那大概占资本的 10%。

turns.en: Yeah, sure.
turns.zh: 嗯，当然。

turns.en: And then we're mostly real estate.
turns.zh: 剩下的我们主要是房地产。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: We have real estate in like 12 states, and that's the majority of the capital. And then we do some public stuff, the art.
turns.zh: 我们在大约 12 个州有房地产，那是资本的大头。然后我们还做一些公开市场的东西，以及艺术品。

turns.en: Another great email that you sent me. I've written a couple of times about electronic arts. I have this great fight, like they went private. Yeah. they have a, you know, 101 put on their bonds and they're like, no, no, no, we're going to defuse our bonds. And they're super long dated. They're issued in like a low rate environment. And so like the defusance is like 60 cents on the dollar, 70 cents on the dollar. And the bondholders thought they were getting 101 and they're really mad and they're suing. But so I wrote about this and you emailed me, I've also defused like $ 200 million of weirdo bonds, which is another email designed to pique my interest.
turns.zh: 你发给我的另一封绝妙邮件。我写过好几次电子艺界（Electronic Arts，EA）。他们有一场很精彩的官司——他们私有化了。是的。他们的债券上有一个 101（面值加 1%）的回售权（put），然后他们说：不不不，我们要对债券做违约置换式的债务解除（defeasance）。这些债券期限非常长，是在低利率环境下发行的。所以这个 defeasance 的成本大概是面值的 60 美分、70 美分。而债券持有人以为自己拿到的是 101，他们非常生气，正在起诉。我写了这件事之后，你给我发邮件说：我也 defease 掉了大约两亿美元的古怪债券——这又是一封专门用来勾起我兴趣的邮件。

turns.en: But you and I do the same thing. You just write about it. I go like, Sure. Get in trouble chasing weird situations.
turns.zh: 但你和我做的是同一件事。你只是把它写出来。我嘛，就是——好，去追这些古怪的特殊情境，然后惹一身麻烦。

turns.en: We both have fun our way. But so you defused $ 200 million of weirdo bonds, which you told me was like six different bonds.
turns.zh: 我们各玩各的，都玩得开心。那你 defease 了两亿美元的古怪债券，你跟我说那是六只不同的债券。

turns.en: I had six bonds, yeah.
turns.zh: 我有六只债券，对。

turns.en: What does that mean that you defused them? Like you were the... Equity owner. You were the equity owner. Equity owner of like, this is like in the real estate business?
turns.zh: 你说你把它们 defease 掉了，这是什么意思？就是说你是……——股权持有人。——你是股权持有人。——股权持有人，比如，这是在房地产业务里？

turns.en: Yeah, pretty sure it was that. You don't like the real estate business?
turns.zh: 对，基本上就是那样。你不喜欢房地产这门生意？

turns.en: No, no, it's fine.
turns.zh: 不不，挺好的。

turns.en: It doesn't matter what the asset is. Imagine any asset that's securitized by, or that's encumbered by a bond.
turns.zh: 资产是什么并不重要。你想象任何一个被债券证券化、或者被债券设定了抵押负担的资产。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: And you put bonds in a trust. that match every month their U.S. Treasury obligation.
turns.zh: 然后你把一批债券放进一个信托里，这些债券每个月的现金流都能对上它原有的美国国债偿付义务。

turns.en: So you have a bond outstanding. Yeah. And you sort of get rid of the obligation of a bond.
turns.zh: 所以你还有一只债券在外面流通。——是的。——然后你就在某种程度上把这个债券的义务给消掉了。

turns.en: The only way you can get a release of a mortgage is if you match monthly payments the next 20 years frequently with U.S. government obligations or Penny Friday or Tennessee Valley Authority. And there's firms that do this. Right.
turns.zh: 想拿到抵押贷款的解除（release），唯一的办法就是让未来二十年的每月还款都能对上——通常是用美国政府债券（U.S. government obligations）、房利美或房地美（Fannie Mae／Freddie Mac），或者田纳西河谷管理局（Tennessee Valley Authority）的债券。有些机构专门做这个生意。对。

turns.en: Like someone will sell you a package of like Treasury strips or something that match all the payments or whatever.
turns.zh: 就是说有人会卖给你一个组合包，比如国债 STRIPS 之类的，正好能对上所有的还款。

turns.en: You have to have the attorneys and accountants on the bond salesman. And it's, Gnarly, and I don't think risky, but difficult, right? We have very low return on brain damage on a lot of stuff we do. And it's pretty good ROE. So we find assets that are in this... He bought a building in 1977 for a million dollars in the Lower East Side or whatever. And he's 87, and he sells it this year for $ 100 million. And he can pay New York taxes, city, state, federal.
turns.zh: 你得配上律师、会计师，还有债券销售员。这活儿很棘手（gnarly），我不觉得有多大风险，但很难，对吧？我们做的很多事情，‘脑损伤回报率’（return on brain damage）非常低，但股本回报率（ROE）相当不错。所以我们找的是这一类资产……比如某人 1977 年花 100 万美元在下东区（Lower East Side）之类的地方买了栋楼，他现在 87 岁了，今年以一亿美元卖掉。他要交纽约市的税、纽约州的税、还有联邦税。

turns.en: Or.
turns.zh: 或者……

turns.en: He could do a 1031 exchange into a piece of real estate with a long lease on it with a pay down, re-advance mortgage. You ever heard of these? No. It's a mortgage that you can 1031 into and have all that $ 99 million of cash equity. Pay down a mortgage as long as there's a dollar left. And then 30 days in, it will re-advance. It's the pay down and the re-advance. And the re-advance is a borrowing against an asset. So it's tax-free. So you're able to enjoy that $ 99 million of equity, of gain, tax-free, and he's 87. If he dies in 10 years and there's 10 years left.
turns.zh: 或者他可以做一个 1031 置换（1031 exchange），换成一份带有长期租约、附带‘先还本、再放款’（pay-down, re-advance）抵押的房地产。这种东西你听说过吗？——没有。——这是一种你可以用 1031 换进去的抵押贷款，让你那 9,900 万美元的现金权益全都用得上。只要还剩一美元，你就把抵押贷款还掉。然后 30 天之后，它会重新放款给你。这就是‘还本’加‘再放款’。再放款是以资产作抵押的借款，所以是免税的。于是你就能免税地享用那 9,900 万美元的权益、那笔增值，而他已经 87 岁了。如果他十年后去世，那就还剩十年。

turns.en: So he sells an asset with $ 99 million of gain. Sure. He buys a $ 100 million asset to get the 1031 treatment, and then he borrows $ 99 million against that.
turns.zh: 所以他卖掉一项有 9,900 万美元增值的资产。——当然。——他买一项一亿美元的资产来享受 1031 的税务待遇，然后再拿它抵押借出 9,900 万美元。

turns.en: It's pre-baked. Right. The $ 99 comes out 30 days out.
turns.zh: 这是预先设计好的。对。那 9,900 万在 30 天后就出来了。

turns.en: Right. Exactly.
turns.zh: 对。没错。

turns.en: So it's pre-baked. And then he hopefully lives a long time. But when he passes, his heirs receive. An equity interest and a piece of property that is not cash flowing because frequently that mortgage will exactly match every lease payment every month. And so markets without cash flows, like if you have a cash flowing piece of real estate, it's not going to sell for a 50 cap. It's not going to sell for a 50 bps cap rate, right? There's like, it bounds reasonability of price. But if you have non-cash flowing equity interest in a building, like People's eyes glaze over. It's hard to.
turns.zh: 所以这是预先设计好的。然后他就盼着自己活得长。但等他去世时，继承人拿到的是一个权益份额，对应的是一处不产生现金流的物业——因为这类抵押贷款常常正好对上每个月的每一笔租金。所以对于没有现金流的资产，市场……如果你有一处能产生现金流的房地产，它不会按 50 个基点的资本化率（cap rate）卖掉，对吧？这就给价格的合理性划了边界。但如果你手上是一栋楼里不产生现金流的权益份额，大家的眼神就开始放空了。这很难……

turns.en: Figure out what it's worth. So you can buy that at like a 50 cap?
turns.zh: ……搞清楚它值多少钱。所以这种东西你能按 50 个基点的 cap rate 买到？

turns.en: No. You can buy it at a discount to the unlevered value after you defease the loan. So you go through all this trouble defeasing the loan. And sometimes weird stuff happens. I had a corporate lease with one of these zero cash flows that I won't name the lessor, but the location had been taken over by an MS-13 affiliate in an American inner city.
turns.zh: 不能。你能买到的是相对于‘把贷款 defease 掉之后的无杠杆价值’的折价。所以你费尽周折把贷款 defease 掉。有时候会发生很怪的事。我有一处企业租约，就是这类零现金流的资产——我就不说出租方是谁了——但那个地点被美国某座内城里的一个 MS-13 分支组织给占了。

turns.en: I'll leave it at that.
turns.zh: 我就说到这儿吧。

turns.en: They sent the police in. They shot the police. They sent a SWAT team in. They shot the SWAT team. This was national news. And it was part of a package of an estate sale of zero cash flow assets. And they didn't want to think about this. They were mourning the passage of their father and wanted to get cash. So I stepped in. We stepped in.
turns.zh: 他们派了警察进去，那些人朝警察开枪。他们派了 SWAT 特警队进去，那些人朝特警队开枪。这是全国性的新闻。而这处资产属于一整套遗产清仓的零现金流资产包。他们不想再去操心这事。他们正在为父亲的离世哀悼，只想拿到现金。所以我插手了。我们插手了。

turns.en: Woodmont did.
turns.zh: Woodmont 接了手。

turns.en: And it had a ground lease, too. So we had to engage in like a four-way negotiation with the lender, the tenant, the ground lease. and finagle, and I think we made like a five X return or something on buying and finagling for two months on a six figure amount. So my job is like extremely gnarly, messy, painful stuff that you make real returns off of. And the loan was non cross collateralized. So if the whole thing is zero, you lose the equity. But that's what I'm always seeking is non cross collateralized leverage, which is the same thing that happened with the other situation.
turns.zh: 而且它还有一个土地租约（ground lease）。所以我们得跟贷款人、承租人、土地租约方来一场四方谈判，各种腾挪（finagle）。我记得我们在一笔六位数的金额上折腾了两个月，赚了大概五倍的回报。所以我的工作就是这种极度棘手、混乱、痛苦的活儿，但你从中能赚到实打实的回报。而且那笔贷款是非交叉抵押的。所以万一整件事归零，你亏掉的只是权益部分。而这正是我一直在找的东西：非交叉抵押的杠杆——跟前面那个情况是一回事。

turns.en: What is the role of the fees? They're basically like you're buying the thing.
turns.zh: 那么这里面费用（或者说摩擦成本）扮演什么角色？基本上就是说你是在买下这个东西。

turns.en: People don't want to think about it. If it's a bank loan with an amount that they say right at $ 700, 000 check and it goes away, people understand that. If it's like you've got to hire all these service providers and it moves around every day what you'd get paid, it's a nightmare.
turns.zh: 大家就是不愿意去想这些。如果是一笔银行贷款，金额明确，你说，给你开张 70 万美元的支票，事情就了结了，大家能理解。但如果变成：你得雇一堆服务提供商，而且你能拿到多少钱每天都在变，那就是一场噩梦。

turns.en: But so like you buy a thing for like $ 100 and it has an $ 80 loan, and so they sell it to you at $ 20, but you can defuse the $ 80 loan for $ 60, and so you make money.
turns.zh: 所以说，比如你花 100 美元买一个东西，它上面有 80 美元的贷款，他们按 20 美元卖给你；但你可以只花 60 美元就把那 80 美元的贷款 defease 掉，于是你就赚到了钱。

turns.en: It's more like you have a thing worth $ 100 and you have an $ 80 loan because of where your interest rates are. You could pay 20 and the loan is actually at 60 now or something. So you can make a return from the headache of the thing.
turns.zh: 更像是这样：你有一个价值 100 美元的东西，上面有 80 美元的贷款——因为利率变了。你可能付 20 美元，而那笔贷款现在的实际价值只有 60 美元之类的。所以你能从这个‘麻烦’本身赚到回报。

turns.en: So you can instead of paying off the loan at 80, you pay it off at 60 by defeasance. Exactly.
turns.zh: 所以你不是按 80 把贷款还清，而是通过 defeasance 按 60 把它了结。——正是。

turns.en: The defeasance is less of a part of it than I might have. It's more like headache than defeasance. The EA defeasance is kind of interesting because it's not that different from the Waters situation where the borrower's argument is going to be, you're still getting your payments every month. The defeasance is still going to pay them every month. the 60 cents on the dollar you said, the payments are exactly identical. That's what a defeasance is.
turns.zh: defeasance 本身在这里的分量，比我原本以为的要小。更多的是‘麻烦’，而不是 defeasance。EA 那个 defeasance 就挺有意思，因为它跟 EA 案的情况没什么两样——借款方的论点会是：你每个月照样收到你的还款。defeasance 信托照样会按月付给他们。你说的那个面值的 60 美分，但每笔还款是完全一样的。这就是 defeasance 的含义。

turns.en: Yes. So where EA is, is they issued these bonds at like, I forget, but like very low rates because it was like in a super low rate environment and they were investment grade. And they issued these 30-year bonds, which as rates went up, traded like, I don't know, 60, 70 cents on the dollar. And then they got bought out in an LBO. And so the bondholders are like, well, you got bought out in an LBO, you got downgraded, probably. And so that triggers a 101 put. So instead of getting These like bonds that are now worth like 60 or whatever, we get 101 right now. And EA says, no, you get defeased.
turns.zh: 对。那 EA 的情况是：他们发行这些债券的时候利率大概是——我忘了——反正非常低，因为当时是超低利率环境，而且他们是投资级。他们发的是 30 年期债券。随着利率上升，这些债券的交易价格跌到……我不知道，面值的六七十美分。然后他们被 LBO（杠杆收购）买走了。所以债券持有人说：你们被 LBO 收购了，评级大概被下调了，那就会触发 101 的回售权。所以，与其拿这些现在只值 60 美分的债券，我们现在就要按 101 拿回本金。而 EA 说：不行，你们拿到的是 defeasance。

turns.en: So you get the exact same. Exactly.
turns.zh: 所以你们拿到的完全一样。——正是。

turns.en: You get the exact payments you're contracted to.
turns.zh: 你拿到的就是合同里约定的那些还款，一分不差。

turns.en: How can you complain if you're getting the exact same payments?
turns.zh: 如果你拿到的还款一模一样，你还有什么好抱怨的？

turns.en: So my understanding is there's two lines of complaint. Most people I talk to think that EA wins, but I really don't know. One line of complaint is that the 101 put is like you get the put if there's a change of control and the company is downgraded or the bonds are downgraded. And EA, part of what they're trying is to not get the bonds downgraded by going to the ratings agencies and saying, look, they're defused. They're like AAA credit.
turns.zh: 据我理解，投诉有两条线。我聊过的大多数人认为 EA 会赢，但我真的说不准。第一条线是：那个 101 回售权的触发条件是发生了控制权变更，并且公司被下调评级或者债券被下调评级。而 EA 在做的一部分努力，就是不让债券被下调评级——他们去找评级机构说：看，这些债券已经 defease 了，它们等于是 AAA 级信用。

turns.en: U.S.
turns.zh: 美国……

turns.en: Government obligations. AA now.
turns.zh: ……政府债券。现在评级是 AA。

turns.en: AA, yeah.
turns.zh: AA，对。

turns.en: But I don't know that that's going to work because... Why wouldn't it?
turns.zh: 但我不知道这招能不能奏效，因为……——为什么不行？

turns.en: In equity, why wouldn't it? If you're going to get the same payments, should there be a windfall? A 40 cent windfall?
turns.zh: 从道理上讲，为什么不行？如果你反正会拿到同样的还款，那还该不该有一笔意外之财（windfall）？一笔 40 美分的意外之财？

turns.en: So this is what I think about. I think a lot of financial instruments in the world are priced because they have some windfall value, right? So, like, I used to do equity derivatives. Where was it, Matt? And there's this trade called the call spread. It's not a call spread. It's called the call options overlay. You do, like, companies issue convertible bonds. They essentially buy back the conversion option, the convertible bond, sell a higher strike call option. And it's like, you know, it's a multi-hundred million dollar transaction. And, you know, it's often competitive and it's priced at a fairly tight rate. And sometimes banks will sell it to you at, like, scratch, like at very, very, very tight rates because... The way it works is that if the company is acquired in a merger, the bank gets a ridiculous windfall. And, like, there have been lawsuits over it. I think that the windfalls have been reduced. But, like, there's this ridiculous windfall. And so if you have a portfolio of calls.
turns.zh: 这就是我会想到的东西。我认为世上很多金融工具之所以是那个价格，是因为它们带有一点‘意外之财’的价值，对吧？比如说，我以前是做股票衍生品（equity derivatives）的。——是在哪家来着，Matt？——有这么一种交易叫看涨价差（call spread）——不，不是看涨价差，叫看涨期权叠加（call options overlay）。是这样的：公司发行可转债（convertible bonds），它们本质上是把转换期权买回来——可转债卖出去，再卖出一个更高行权价的看涨期权。这是一笔好几亿美元的交易。而且往往是竞争性报价，定价定得很紧。有时候银行会以‘零利润’（scratch）的价格卖给你，就是非常、非常、非常紧的费率，因为……它的机制是：如果这家公司在并购中被收购，银行就能拿到一笔荒唐的意外之财。而且为此打过官司。我觉得这类意外之财已经被削减了。但总之，就是这么一笔荒唐的意外之财。所以如果你手上有一篮子看涨期权……

turns.en: The portfolio should be cheaper because there's some windfalls throughout.
turns.zh: ……那这个组合就应该更便宜，因为里面散布着一些意外之财。

turns.en: And so you can be like, well, if I, you know, and people don't literally do this, but you can be like, I'll sell 20 call spreads. I'll price them all at scratch. I'll make all my money on the one company that gets taken out. And I have to imagine that, like, there's just a teeny element of that. in bond investing, right?
turns.zh: 所以你可以这么想——大家实际上不会真这么干，但你可以这么想：我卖 20 个看涨价差，全部按零利润定价，我所有的钱都靠那一家被收购的公司来赚。我可以想象，债券投资里也有那么一点点这种成分，对吧？

turns.en: We're like- But don't you think they're also hedging the interest rates, like the broad interest rates? Because what happened to the spreads on EA bonds? So if broad interest rates went up.
turns.zh: 我们就像……但你不觉得他们其实也在对冲利率吗？我是说广义的利率？因为 EA 债券的利差后来怎么样了？如果广义利率上升——

turns.en: Their spreads, like, I mean, it's hard to say what happened to the spreads because it's all in the– but, like, their spreads should have gotten wider because they got LBO'd. But then they should go narrow again because they're getting defused.
turns.zh: 它们的利差，我是说，很难讲利差到底发生了什么，因为全都混在 defeasance 信托里了；但是，它们的利差本来应该因为被 LBO 而变宽，然后又要因为被 defease 而重新收窄。

turns.en: The windfall comes from the fact that rates– Yeah, sure, sure, sure.
turns.zh: 这笔意外之财是因为利率……——是是是，当然当然。

turns.en: It's just a windfall. It's like windfalls go from windfalls.
turns.zh: 它就是一笔意外之财。就是说，意外之财会生出意外之财。

turns.en: We're allocating the windfall.
turns.zh: 我们在分配这笔意外之财。

turns.en: Yeah, we're allocating the windfall. I don't know if the bondholders had rates, right? I mean, like, it's a– you know, it's a long-only investor. It's like they buy these bonds. Rates go up. They lose a lot of money on the bonds. And then, whoops, you get 101 back.
turns.zh: 对，我们在分配这笔意外之财。我不知道债券持有人有没有对冲利率，对吧？我是说，这是一个……你知道，这是个只做多头（long-only）的投资人。他们买入这些债券，利率上涨，他们在债券上亏了很多钱。然后——哎哟——你能拿回 101。

turns.en: You thought EA wins? You think the defeasance holds?
turns.zh: 你认为 EA 会赢？你觉得这个 defeasance 站得住？

turns.en: I don't want to speculate on it because I truly don't know. But my gut and what most people tell me is probably EA wins.
turns.zh: 我不想瞎猜，因为我真的不知道。但我的直觉、以及大多数人告诉我的，大概是 EA 会赢。

turns.en: Can't you imagine a trial like your honor? They're getting all the payments.
turns.zh: 你能想象庭审现场吗？‘法官大人，他们拿到了所有的还款。

turns.en: If the U.S.
turns.zh: 只要美国……

turns.en: Government still pays dollars on treasury bonds, they're going to get all the payments. Where's the damage? I'm not saying that's a winning argument.
turns.zh: ……政府还在为国债支付美元，他们就会拿到所有的还款。损害在哪儿？’我不是说这是个能赢的论点。

turns.en: That's not how bonds work. Because it's not an equity, right? I know. I know.
turns.zh: 债券不是这么运作的。因为它不是股权，对吧？——我知道，我知道。

turns.en: It's a contract.
turns.zh: 它是一份合同。

turns.en: Whatever it says. And sometimes you can get windfalls. I know.
turns.zh: 合同怎么写就怎么算。而且有时候你就是能拿到意外之财。——我知道。

turns.en: I didn't go to Yale Law School, but I know that.
turns.zh: 我没上过耶鲁法学院，但这个道理我还是懂的。

turns.en: Where did you go to law school? Do you remember? I do not.
turns.zh: 那你上的哪所法学院？——你还记得吗？——我记不得了。

turns.en: I went to Harvard Law School. I didn't ever take the bar. I'm a lawyer, but not an attorney.
turns.zh: 我上的是哈佛法学院（Harvard Law School）。我从来没考过律师执照考试（bar）。我是个法律人（lawyer），但不是执业律师（attorney）。

turns.en: Isn't that what we have to say now? I've never believed that that is a real distinction, but people do. I don't know. I don't know which one's which or whatever.
turns.zh: 现在是不是都得这么说？我从来不相信这两者之间真有什么区别，但大家确实这么分。我不知道。我搞不清哪个是哪个，随便吧。

turns.en: I've said that for a decade since I never took the bar.
turns.zh: 自从没考过执照，这句话我已经说了十年了。

turns.en: For all I know, that's the correct distinction.
turns.zh: 说不定这就是那个正确的区分呢。

turns.en: I don't know if it's the correct distinction.
turns.zh: 我不知道它是不是正确的区分。

turns.en: Do you think that your legal training is useful to you in your current job, or was it strictly recreational? Hesitating a disappointingly long time for law schools.
turns.zh: 你觉得你受的法律训练在你现在的工作里是有用的，还是纯属娱乐性质？——为一个上过法学院的人犹豫这么久，真令人失望。

turns.en: I was looking for weirdo investment work in 2009. It was a really hard time to look for work. I graduated in 2010 and had a chemistry degree. You had a classic degree, so you understand having a little bit off the beaten path.
turns.zh: 2009 年我在找那种古怪的投资类工作，那是个非常难找工作的时期。我 2010 年毕业，拿的是化学学位。——你拿的是古典学学位，所以你能理解那种稍微偏离主流路线的感觉。

turns.en: And so this is reminding me that one of my bosses at Goldman years later, I had lunch with him and he was like a partner at Goldman and made a lot of money and was like in his fifties. He was like, I'm thinking about going.
turns.zh: 这让我想起来，多年以后我在高盛（Goldman）的一位老板——我跟他吃过午饭，他是高盛的合伙人，赚了很多钱，五十多岁——他说：我在考虑要不要去……

turns.en: To law school.
turns.zh: ……上法学院。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Well, my boss asked him, I'm going to take the bar now. Like I was like, no, no, it's worked out. It was my least dirty shirt. After graduating with a chemistry degree, like I took the GRE, I took the GMAT, I took the LSAT. I got a whole bunch of business schools. I got a bunch of law schools. Harvard Law School sounds nice. It's right across the street. So it's right next to the chemistry department.
turns.zh: 结果我那位老板对他说：‘我现在要去考执照了。’我当时想：不不，事情都已经成了。那可是我手里最不脏的一件衬衫。化学系毕业之后，我考了 GRE、考了 GMAT、考了 LSAT。我拿到了一堆商学院的录取，也拿到了一堆法学院的录取。哈佛法学院听起来不错。就在街对面。就在化学系隔壁。

turns.en: This is what you do with a classics degree is you.
turns.zh: 拿了古典学学位的人就是这么干的，你会……

turns.en: Go to law school. Same with the chemistry degree unless you want to get a PhD, which I thought about.
turns.zh: ……去上法学院。化学学位也一样，除非你想去读博士——我倒是想过。

turns.en: I thought about the classics PhD.
turns.zh: 我考虑过读古典学博士。

turns.en: I worked for a Nobel laureate in undergrad. I washed dishes for a Nobel laureate for $ 100 an hour. That's how I paid my way to Harvard undergrad.
turns.zh: 本科的时候我给一位诺贝尔奖得主打工。我给一位诺奖得主洗盘子，一小时 100 美元。我读哈佛本科的钱就是这么挣出来的。

turns.en: Can't do that in classics. Wait, do you want to talk about Mark Walter, Todd Boley?
turns.zh: 古典学里可没这种好事。等等，你要不要聊聊 Mark Walter 和 Todd Boehly？

turns.en: It's interesting.
turns.zh: 这挺有意思。

turns.en: Like these guys, this is like the business model.
turns.zh: 这些人，这就是那种商业模式。

turns.en: Of Berkshire Hathaway.
turns.zh: 伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）的商业模式。

turns.en: Yes. Like I've mentioned the Berkshire Hathaway business model of like, there are people in the world, Warren Buffett, Todd Boley, Mark Walter, the guys who run Apollo who are like, we're really good investors. And one side of that is finding good investments, and the other side of it is finding good funding. And there's no better funding than life insurance liabilities.
turns.zh: 对。我提过伯克希尔·哈撒韦的商业模式：世上有那么一些人——沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）、Todd Boehly、Mark Walter、还有执掌 Apollo 的那几位——他们的态度是：我们是非常优秀的投资人。这件事的一半是找到好的投资标的，另一半是找到好的资金来源。而没有什么资金来源比寿险负债更好了。

turns.en: I think there's one important difference. Berkshire and National Divinity are based in– do you know what state they're all based in and under the insurance regulation of?
turns.zh: 我觉得有一个重要区别。伯克希尔和 National Indemnity（全国赔偿保险公司）都注册在——你知道它们全都注册在哪个州、受哪个州的保险监管吗？

turns.en: I was assuming it was Nebraska. Yes, Nebraska.
turns.zh: 我猜是内布拉斯加州（Nebraska）。——对，内布拉斯加。

turns.en: And there's a bunch of insurance companies in Nebraska. These other insurance companies– Berkshire.
turns.zh: 内布拉斯加有一大堆保险公司。这些别的保险公司——伯克希尔……

turns.en: Is not like– Like there's huge property and casualty, which is like a different.
turns.zh: ……可不一样。伯克希尔有巨大的财产险和意外险（property & casualty）业务，那是另一种东西。

turns.en: It is very different business model. But there's an important thing. You have the float in Nebraska. I believe you can invest the float in equities. And that's allowed and blessed and fine.
turns.zh: 确实是非常不同的商业模式。但有一点很重要。你在内布拉斯加有浮存金（float）。我相信你可以把浮存金投在股票上。这是被允许的、被认可的、没问题的。

turns.en: Buy shares of Coke.
turns.zh: 去买可口可乐的股票。

turns.en: Yeah, Coca-Cola or any other thing and buy shares of a chocolate company, any other thing. What Mark Walters and the guy today, what's his name? Todd Bowley.
turns.zh: 对，可口可乐，或者任何别的东西；买一家巧克力公司的股票，随便什么。而 Mark Walter 和今天那位——他叫什么来着？Todd Boehly。

turns.en: I read about it today. We were doing it on Wednesday. Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: 我今天刚读到。我们周三那期就写了这个。是啊是啊。

turns.en: What they did was set up an insurer, issue a bunch of annuities, which Apollo also, Athene, also got deep into annuities, which I'm interested in why they both picked annuities and how bad some of the annuities turned out for the annuitants. But then they borrowed money from the insurer, right? The insurer had an asset and liability of the annuities, but it had an asset of a loan. That's different, right? turns.zh: 他们干的事情是：设立一家保险公司，发行一大堆年金（annuities）——Apollo 旗下的 Athene 也深陷年金业务，我很感兴趣为什么他们都选了年金，以及这些年金对年金持有人来说最后变得多糟糕。但接着他们从这家保险公司借钱，对吧？保险公司有年金这项负债，但同时也有一笔贷款资产。这就不一样了，对吧？这跟直接持有股权投资、享受浮存金的上行收益，本质上是不同的，不是吗？

turns.en: Yeah, sure.
turns.zh: 嗯，当然。

But because you can duration match, there's this game you could play with length of the loan, right? Yeah. If you make little bitty loans, then you don't have to have very much capital held against it because it rolls off in three months.
turns.zh: 因为你可以做久期匹配（duration match）。我觉得这才是真正的关键点：你可以做久期匹配，对吧？但正因为你能做久期匹配，在贷款期限上就有一个可以玩的游戏，对吧？——嗯。——如果你放的是很短的小额贷款，你就不需要为它计提太多资本，因为它三个月就到期滚掉了。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: But if it's to the boss, the guy that owns it, isn't going to keep rolling.
turns.zh: 但如果借款人是老板本人、是那个拥有它的人，那就不会一直滚下去。

turns.en: I read about it the other day. There's one part of Mark Walter's insurance empire is that he was making– or these insurance companies were making these short-term loans that rolled every six months. That turned out to be affiliate transactions. And so you wonder like.
turns.zh: 我前几天读到过。Mark Walter 保险帝国的一个部分是：他——或者说这些保险公司——在放这种每六个月滚动一次的短期贷款。结果发现这些是关联方交易（affiliate transactions）。所以你会想……

turns.en: Why– Because they got a lower capital charge, right?
turns.zh: 为什么……因为这样资本计提更低，对吧？

turns.en: Yes. I mean the answer is– I definitely have lenders.
turns.zh: 对。我是说答案就是——我确实有贷款人会这么干。

turns.en: I have thought about that. We have a bunch of different loans against a bunch of assets. That's the thing that's come up repeatedly is if they're short-term loans, yeah, we'll roll them, we'll roll them, but it has a lower capital charge for them if it's short-term loans.
turns.zh: 我想到过这一点。我们有一堆针对不同资产的贷款。反复出现的情况就是：如果是短期贷款，行，我们会滚续、我们会滚续；但对他们来说，短期贷款的资本计提更低。

turns.en: So a lender says to you, I would rather be on you this money for six months than five years.
turns.zh: 所以贷款人会跟你说：我更愿意把这笔钱借给你六个月，而不是五年。

turns.en: And don't worry about it.
turns.zh: 而且‘别担心’。

turns.en: We'll roll it. Don't worry about it. We'll roll it. Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: ‘我们会滚续的。别担心。我们会滚续的。’是是是。

turns.en: I mean, I don't have that. You have that over the phone, right?
turns.zh: 我是说，我手上可没有这种书面承诺。这种话是在电话里说的，对吧？

turns.en: Right. No, I've read about this. There's the Greensill, the supply chain finance guys. They were making these receivables loans to companies that didn't have the receivables.
turns.zh: 对。不，我读到过这个。就是 Greensill——那家供应链金融公司。他们向一些公司发放应收账款贷款，而那些公司根本没有应收账款。

turns.en: They were like, one day we'll make a sale.
turns.zh: 他们的意思是：总有一天我们会做出一笔销售的。

turns.en: And the borrower- When Greensill collapsed, the state was like, all right, pay those loans. And the borrower was like, no, no, no.
turns.zh: 而借款人——当 Greensill 倒闭时，那边说：好了，把这些贷款还上吧。借款人却说：不不不。

turns.en: We didn't even have revenue.
turns.zh: 我们连营收都没有。

turns.en: You told me you'd roll these forever. No, they wouldn't roll them forever.
turns.zh: 你们跟我说过会永远滚续的。——不，他们可不会永远滚续。

turns.en: You can't rely on that. I'm not saying I've relied on it. I'm saying that's a conversation that's come up before.
turns.zh: 你不能指望这个。我不是说我指望过它，我是说这样的对话以前确实出现过。

turns.en: That's interesting. Do other people rely? It must be.
turns.zh: 这有意思。别人会指望吗？肯定是有的。

turns.en: Sure. This guy did.
turns.zh: 当然。这位就指望了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: So just to be clear, so Nebraska is really good from an insurance perspective because they allow you to invest in equities, and especially I think microcap equities as the float. in a way that Buffett couldn't get margin loans or any other financing. And insurance served as leverage, as effectively fixed-rate leverage, because you could look at what the combined ratio was, and it served as fixed-rate leverage for investing in microcap equities. I'm not from Nebraska. I'm from Arkansas. And Arkansas has really entrepreneurial lending rules. The banking rules in Arkansas are exciting. I'm from a town of 10,000 people. There's five banks headquartered in my hometown. And I have a Harvard Law degree. And you walk in and shake the hand and look in the eye of the CEO or chief lending officer. Anybody that has a $ 5 million net worth will set up a bank because they can borrow 20 to 1 commercial deposits against it and make higher rate loans against. That's when I started this business. I didn't have any money. I started this business with $ 8, 000. And we were borrowed from intelligent, entrepreneurial chief lending officers of these small banks in Arkansas to do weirdo real estate investments. And we were able to get 90, 97% LTV loans against busted weird real estate because they charged me out the nose and because they have the ability to effectively write high-field, personally guaranteed loans from the Arkansas banks. You don't do it with 70% of your equity capital if you're the bank.
turns.zh: 所以说清楚一点：从保险的角度看，内布拉斯加真的很好，因为他们允许你把浮存金投在股票上，尤其是微盘股（microcap）——这是巴菲特当年靠保证金贷款或任何其他融资都拿不到的。保险起到了杠杆的作用，实际上是固定利率的杠杆，因为你可以看综合成本率（combined ratio）是多少；它为投资微盘股提供了固定利率的杠杆。我不是内布拉斯加人，我是阿肯色州人。阿肯色的放贷规则非常有创业精神。阿肯色的银行规则很刺激。我来自一个只有一万人的小镇，我老家镇上就有五家银行的总部。而我有一个哈佛法学学位。你走进去，跟 CEO 或者首席信贷官握个手、看着对方的眼睛——任何有 500 万美元净资产的人都会去开一家银行，因为他们可以按 20 比 1 借入商业存款，然后拿去放利率更高的贷款。这就是我开始这门生意的时候。我当时一分钱都没有。我用 8,000 美元起步。我们从阿肯色这些小银行里那些聪明、有创业精神的首席信贷官那里借钱，去做古怪的房地产投资。我们能拿到 90%、97% 贷款价值比（LTV）的贷款，抵押品是那些破败古怪的房地产——因为他们收我的利息非常狠，也因为他们有能力实质上发放高额、带个人担保的贷款，由阿肯色的银行出资。如果你是银行，你不会用自己的股权资本的 70% 去干这个。

turns.en: They do it with some.
turns.zh: 有些银行确实会拿一部分自有资金这么干。

turns.en: That's how I started, though.
turns.zh: 不过我就是这样起步的。

turns.en: So, like, I think of, like, Warren Buffett and Mark Waltz. Like, these are, like.
turns.zh: 所以我会想到沃伦·巴菲特和 Mark Walter，这些人是那种……

turns.en: They're from different states.
turns.zh: 他们来自不同的州。

turns.en: Big operators.
turns.zh: 大玩家。

turns.en: They're not from Arkansas.
turns.zh: 他们不是阿肯色人。

turns.zh: 但是这些阿肯色佬，他们就是那种人……——是做牙医赚了钱的？——是农民。——农民，好，他们是种地赚了些钱。

turns.en: They could still be quite sophisticated. It wouldn't be insane if you had a diversified loan portfolio from a lending officer to make some weirdo loans. And if you're going to make some weirdo loans to raise the overall ROA of your bank, pick the poor, hungry, determined. Or it's a PhD, poor, hungry, driven. 25-year-old Harvard, Harvard guy from a town of 160 down the road and ride him alone to do some weird stuff.
turns.zh: 他们照样可以非常老练。如果一个信贷官手里有一个多元化的贷款组合，去放一些古怪的贷款并不疯狂。而如果你要放一些古怪的贷款来提高整个银行的资产回报率（ROA），那就挑那种穷的、饿的、有决心的；或者是个博士、穷、饿、有闯劲的 25 岁哈佛小伙——来自 160 英里外的小镇——让他一个人去干点古怪的事。

turns.en: So you did like a little like barn swimming tour of Arkansas banks to raise money for your weirdo real estate? I still do. Yeah.
turns.zh: 所以你就这么在阿肯色各家银行之间来了一趟‘谷仓巡回’（barnstorming tour），为你的古怪房地产项目融资？——我现在还在这么干。——是啊。

turns.en: All the time. They're great guys.
turns.zh: 一直都在干。他们都是很棒的人。

turns.zh: 所以那就是你的资金来源？

turns.zh: 最初是。现在我们已经做得足够大，很多事情上我们拿到的是全国性和国际性的无追索权贷款方（lenders）。

turns.en: Not all.
turns.zh: 不是全部？

turns.en: Mostly.
turns.zh: 大部分是。

turns.en: It's mostly real estate that you're not like.
turns.zh: 主要是房地产，你不是那种……

turns.zh: 我们大部分资产是房地产。

turns.zh: 你在高盛有主经纪商（prime brokerage）服务吗？

turns.zh: 不在高盛。我有好几家主经纪商。我们做很多公开市场的东西。所以总归是有的。

turns.zh: 我们接下来聊点什么？

turns.zh: 我们要不要聊聊 SpaceX 跟特斯拉（Tesla）合并的事？

turns.en: Oh, yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，对。

turns.en: Flying cars.
turns.zh: 飞行汽车。

turns.en: Flying cars. With SpaceX, what do you think?
turns.zh: 飞行汽车。关于 SpaceX，你怎么看？

turns.en: I'm too dumb to have an opinion, but it's interesting to see. You have like a very, very controlled thing merging with like a pretty well-controlled thing. From a corporate governance perspective, it's like a mess. isn't it?
turns.zh: 我太笨了，没什么观点，但看着挺有意思。你有一个非常、非常受控的东西，跟一个相当受控的东西合并。从公司治理的角度看，这就是一团乱麻，不是吗？

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, the thing I wrote is that it's a mess anyway. Like it's a mess to have the two companies. Like it's less messy to have one company because like if you just wave a wand, have one company, then this guy who is clearly the decision maker of the company gets to decide on strategy and he gets to decide on capital allocation. He gets to decide on like what the priorities are and then just turn the company in that direction. And when you have two companies, When he's deciding, like, this is how we're going to pursue AI, that means one company loses out.
turns.zh: 是啊。我写的那篇是说：反正本来就已经很乱了。有两家公司本来就乱。合成一家公司反而没那么乱，因为如果你挥一挥魔杖、变成一家公司，那么这位显然是公司决策者的人就可以决定战略，可以决定资本配置，可以决定优先级是什么，然后把公司朝那个方向转。而当你有两家公司的时候，当他在决定‘我们该这么做 AI’的时候，就意味着其中一家要吃亏。

turns.en: But didn't we have a problem with SolarCity with the correct allocation of economics?
turns.zh: 但我们不是在 SolarCity 那件事上遇到过问题吗？就是经济利益的正确分配。

turns.en: No, sure, sure, sure. The actual, like, the merger is a nightmare. Except it's not really. So SolarCity is tough because, like, Tesla acquired SolarCity, which was, like, another Elon Musk company. And the Musks owned different amounts of, so there's, like, a conflict there. But it's also, like, there were allegations that SolarCity was, like, on its way to bankruptcy.
turns.zh: 不，当然当然。实际的合并过程才是噩梦。不过也不完全是。SolarCity 那个很棘手，因为特斯拉收购了 SolarCity，而那是马斯克的另一家公司，而且马斯克家族各方持股比例不同，所以那里存在利益冲突。但同时也有一种说法，指 SolarCity 当时正走向破产。

turns.en: Weren't they in financial distress? I didn't have a position.
turns.zh: 他们不是陷入财务困境了吗？——我当时没有持仓。

turns.en: So that was like a really fraught one. This is like these two giant public companies, right? Like you could just like pick a day, look at the market caps. That's your exchange ratio. It's easy. I know that you can't actually do that. You need to like have a special committee and have a fairness opinion, but it's like fine. It's fine.
turns.zh: 所以那个案子非常棘手。而现在这是两家巨型上市公司，对吧？你随便挑一天，看看两边的市值，那就是你的换股比例。很容易。我知道你实际上不能这么干，你得设一个特别委员会、拿一份公允性意见（fairness opinion），但基本上没什么问题。没问题的。

turns.en: Are you arguing that the price of Tesla and the price of SpaceX are efficient?
turns.zh: 你的意思是特斯拉的价格和 SpaceX 的价格都是有效的（efficient）？

turns.en: I guess you are.
turns.zh: 我想是吧。

turns.en: You're assuming that.
turns.zh: 你这是在假设这一点。

turns.en: I would say that there is a large cloud of uncertainty around both of them and there's no A prior reason to think that like one is high and one is low, right? Like maybe they're both high, maybe they're both low, but like the idea that like the market systematically overvalues Tesla and undervalues SpaceX or vice versa. It's like, yeah, why? Okay.
turns.zh: 我会说，两者头上都笼罩着一大片不确定性的云，而且没有任何先验的理由认为其中一个偏高、另一个偏低，对吧？也许两个都偏高，也许两个都偏低。但要说市场系统性地高估特斯拉、低估 SpaceX，或者反过来——嗯，凭什么？好吧。

turns.en: I like that. I've read your article.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。我读过你那篇文章。

turns.en: And by the way, like, I think like, like if you're like an index fund and you own a lot of Tesla and you own zero SpaceX, you'll complain, right? Like you could have it, but like if you're like a, you know, Elon Musk retail shareholder, it's great. It's fine. Whatever. We've been in it at a par exchange ratio. That's fine.
turns.zh: 而且顺便说一句，我觉得如果你是指数基金、持有大量特斯拉而完全不持有 SpaceX，你会抱怨，对吧？你本来可以拥有它的。但如果你是那种马斯克的散户股东，那就太好了。没问题。随便。反正一直是按平价换股比例来的。那就行。

turns.en: How does it work for my queues? You don't want to talk about the queues?
turns.zh: 那这些 Qs 怎么算？你不想聊聊 Qs 吗？

turns.en: What about the queues? They're cheap. It's interesting. Queues are cheap. I feel like this is not that kind of podcast.
turns.zh: Qs 怎么了？它们很便宜。挺有意思的。Qs 很便宜。我感觉这不像是那种会聊这个的播客。

turns.en: Scratch it.
turns.zh: 那就划掉。

turns.en: Move on. Why are the queues cheap? Tell me.
turns.zh: 换个话题。为什么 Qs 便宜？跟我说说。

People are jumping out of windows, right? Since July. The P of the Qs has gone down 40%. That's weird. It's growing really fast. It sure looks like it's going to go fast next year if all the numbers are right, but who knows?
turns.zh: 如果你有一只股票、或者整个市场跌了 40%，那每天都会上报纸头条。‘崩盘了’。所有人都在恐慌，有人在跳楼，对吧？而从七月到现在，Qs 的 P（价格）已经跌了 40%。这很奇怪。它增长得非常快。如果所有数字都对的话，明年看起来肯定会跑得快，但谁知道呢？

turns.en: The P has gone down 40%, meaning the E has gone up a lot. Yeah.
turns.zh: P 跌了 40%，意思是 E（盈利）涨了很多。——是的。

turns.en: P's gone up a little. E's gone up a lot.
turns.zh: P 涨了一点，E 涨了很多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: It has the flavor. But like, I mean, the E is like, there's like, yeah, like people are putting a broader like cloud of uncertainty around the earnings, right? Because like.
turns.zh: 是有那个味道。但是，我是说，那个 E……是啊，大家是在给盈利罩上一层更宽的不确定性的云，对吧？因为……

turns.en: 40% is a lot, man.
turns.zh: 40% 已经很多了，兄弟。

turns.en: Yeah. Okay.
turns.zh: 嗯。好吧。

turns.en: 28 to 20. I'm not smart enough to have an opinion about those. Sorry.
turns.zh: 从 28 倍到 20 倍。我没聪明到能对它们有观点。抱歉。

turns.zh: 我同意它有崩盘的味道，但这不代表它就便宜了。

turns.zh: 这两点我都认。

turns.zh: 嗯，嗯。没错。确实有那个味道。

turns.zh: 也许‘便宜’这个说法也对。真是不同寻常。

turns.zh: 是啊，但这是不同寻常的时代，对吧？我是说，盈利增长本身就很不同寻常。

turns.zh: 这真的很怪，对吧？标普 500（S&P 500）的每股收益（EPS）三季度对三季度同比涨了大概……多少来着，40% 左右。

turns.en: By the way, the other thing I'll say about that is like, so some of the E is like moving up enormous quantities of CapEx or whatever, but some of it is- It's.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，关于这一点我还要说的是：一部分 E 是把巨额资本开支（capex）提前挪上来之类的，但另一部分是——是……

turns.zh: ……就是借钱把一切都往前挪，对吧？

turns.zh: 还有一部分是所持资产估值的上升，对吧？

turns.en: You've got to count those out. Don't look at the Anthropic increasing the E of Google. It's like after you correct that.
turns.zh: 你得把那些剔除掉。别把 Anthropic 抬高了谷歌（Google）的 E 这件事算进去。得在你调整之后再看。

turns.en: Okay, after you correct that. You've got to correct that. That's not.
turns.zh: 好，调整之后。你确实得调整。那不是……

turns.en: I can't correct that. In, like, 1989, I was, like, 11 years old.
turns.zh: 我调整不了。1989 年那会儿，我才 11 岁。

turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: Is this what it felt like? What year did you graduate?
turns.zh: 当时就是这种感觉吗？你哪年毕业的？

turns.en: I was in college. I was a classics major. I was not following the math back.
turns.zh: 我当时还在上大学。我是古典学专业的。那会儿我没在关注市场。

turns.en: You taught, then, while I was, then, walked out of Goldman. So you didn't start at Goldman until, like, what?
turns.zh: 所以你……而我后来从高盛出来了。那你是什么时候才进高盛的？大概是哪年？

turns.en: Oh, seven.
Oh, wow.
turns.zh: 哦，哇。

turns.en: It was great. That's a great time.
turns.zh: 那很棒。那是个很好的时候。

turns.en: It was great.
turns.zh: 确实很棒。

turns.en: It was great. Here's why it was great. One, I didn't get fired. And I was like, well, I'm safe because like, if I was going to get fired, I'd have been fired by now. And two, and it wasn't that great, but in retrospect, I was fascinated by it. Like I didn't do anything for six months. Like, From September 08 to, like, March 09, like, we did no deals. We did nothing. And I don't know what I did all day.
turns.zh: 确实很棒。我说说为什么棒。第一，我没被炒鱿鱼。我当时想：好，我安全了，因为如果要被炒，我早就被炒了。第二——其实没那么棒，但回头看我觉得很有意思——我大概有六个月什么都没干。从 2008 年 9 月到 2009 年 3 月左右，我们一单交易都没做。什么都没做。我都不知道自己整天在干什么。

turns.en: You can't find something smart to do when everything's falling apart? It's really that capital markets driven?
turns.zh: 当一切都在崩塌的时候，你就找不到什么聪明的事情可做吗？这真的是完全由资本市场驱动的吗？

turns.en: It was corporate equity. So, like, I'm sure, like, the flow people were trading options. But, like, I was doing, like, equity derivatives is a different word. Like, it's really, like, oriented around the convertible bond market. And the convertible bond market was shut. And we did kind of reopen it. We, like … It's such a weird trade. Like, the convertible bond market shot for a while for reasons including, like, some hedge funds lost their shirts. There were, like, laws against short selling, so, like, convertible arbitrage.
turns.zh: 那是公司股权业务（corporate equity）。所以我敢肯定，流量交易那帮人（flow people）当时还在交易期权。但我做的股票衍生品是另一个概念，它其实主要围绕可转债市场。而可转债市场当时是关门的。后来我们算是把它重新打开了。那真是一笔很怪的交易。可转债市场关闭了一段时间，原因包括一些对冲基金亏得血本无归，还有当时有禁止卖空的规定，所以可转债套利（convertible arbitrage）……

turns.en: Oh, wow. I didn't think about that. That applied to convertible arbitrage?
turns.zh: 哦，哇。我没想到这一点。那个禁令也影响可转债套利？

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. It's nuts. Nuts. Okay. Like, truly nuts. But so, like, the convert market was in real bad shape for a while. And one thing that reopened it is that TARP, you know, the financial bailouts, warren buffett did a few trades that were like we buy preferred stocks and we get warrants and then like tarp did the same thing and so there's this template of investors meaning like the government or warren buffett or rescue answers would buy preferred stock with warrants as a thing that could still go on even in the depths of the crisis and so like we did one or two trades like that like in 09 where it's like oh we'll sell you preferred stock and warrants and like you did no no like we did public ones we did a public one and i think there's like more than one of them i think like people were like oh like preferred stock and warrants is a thing so we'll uh we'll do some of those trades.
turns.zh: 对，对。太疯了。疯了。好，真的是疯了。总之，可转债市场有相当长一段时间状况很糟。而重新打开它的一个原因是 TARP——你知道的，那些金融救助。巴菲特做了几笔交易，模式是：我们买优先股，同时拿到认股权证（warrants）；然后 TARP 也做了同样的事。于是就有了这么一个模板：投资人——也就是政府、或者沃伦·巴菲特、或者救援方——会买带认股权证的优先股，即使在危机最深处这依然行得通。所以我们在 2009 年做了一两笔这样的交易，就是‘哦，我们卖给你优先股加认股权证’。——你们做过吗？——不不，我们做的是公开发行的，我们做过一笔公开交易，我记得不止一笔。大家就想：哦，原来‘优先股加认股权证’是个可行的东西，那我们也来做几笔这种交易。

turns.en: You can't remember i never had a job so every day when i get up and there's nothing to do i had a deputy income for like five months in 2013. I was looking for something weird to go do, which is I, you know, look at these pipes or go to an art fair or try to figure something out.
turns.zh: 你都不记得了。我从没有过一份正经工作，所以每天起床都没有事做。2013 年我有大约五个月没有正经工作、只有零星收入。我在那段时间到处找点古怪的事情做，也就是——你知道——去看看这些 PIPE，或者去逛艺术博览会，或者想办法搞明白点什么。

turns.en: Don't get me wrong. When I spent six months never doing a trade at Goldman, like we weren't.
turns.zh: 别误会我。我在高盛有六个月一单交易都没做成，但我们并不是（闲着）……

turns.en: What'd you do all day?
turns.zh: 那你整天都在干什么？

turns.en: I don't remember.
turns.zh: 我不记得了。

turns.en: You read Bloomberg.
turns.zh: 你在看彭博终端。

turns.en: No, like we like worked frantically to try to do it.
turns.zh: 不，我们是在疯狂地努力想把交易做成。

turns.en: I don't know. I don't know.
turns.zh: 我不知道，我不知道。

turns.en: We like made lists. We like called people. We like did a bunch of frantic nonsense that went nowhere. Or like, you know, we like sat around in the lab being like, what can we do? To sell convertible bonds when all the hedge funds blew up and there's no short selling. I like that. I don't remember. It was not a restful time. We probably took a few long lunches, but not very many, considering there were six months of doing no business.
turns.zh: 我们会列清单，会给别人打电话，会做一大堆疯狂的、毫无结果的蠢事。或者，你知道，我们就坐在‘实验室’（lab）里想：我们还能干点什么？在所有对冲基金都爆掉、又不许卖空的情况下，怎么把可转债卖出去。我喜欢那段日子。我不记得了。那绝不是一段清闲的时光。我们大概吃过几次长午餐，但不多——毕竟那六个月一单生意都没做。

turns.en: Must have been so much fun you decided to go do a blog.
turns.zh: 那一定太好玩了，好玩到你决定去写博客。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Can't tell you a good thing?
turns.zh: 就不能说点好听的？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: I subscribed to the Bloomberg Terminal today for the first time. Yeah, I signed up.
turns.zh: 我今天第一次订阅了彭博终端（Bloomberg Terminal）。是的，我注册了。

turns.en: I have a commission.
turns.zh: 我可是有佣金的。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: You told me I'd get it.
turns.zh: 你跟我说过我会拿到的。

turns.en: Free if I came on the podcast. No, kidding, kidding, kidding.
turns.zh: ……说我来上这个播客就免费给我。——不不，开玩笑，开玩笑，开玩笑。

turns.en: You subscribed for the vast quantity of data.
turns.zh: 你是为了那海量的数据才订阅的。

turns.en: Data, yeah. We kept having to recreate things, and we are busy enough, and my Chief Joseph Officer's time is valuable enough now.
turns.zh: 数据，对。我们总是不得不自己重新造一遍数据，而我们又足够忙，而且我的‘首席 Joseph 官’（Chief Joseph Officer）现在的时间也足够值钱了。

turns.en: Chief Joseph Officer.
turns.zh: ‘首席 Joseph 官’。

turns.en: If all the Josephs, he's number one.
turns.zh: 在所有的 Joseph 里面，他排第一。

turns.en: Just one. I hired a guy out of Brooke.
turns.zh: 就一个。我从 Brooke 那儿招了个人。

turns.en: He's really good. And then I have an EA and we called an analyst, but now he's a business manager. His time is too valuable to continue to like crunch numbers. When I mean, the Bloomberg is.
turns.zh: 他非常能干。然后我有一个行政助理（EA），我们本来叫他分析师，但现在他是业务经理了。他的时间太宝贵，不适合再去算数字。我说的是，彭博终端……

turns.en: That's great.
turns.zh: 那很好啊。

turns.en: It's underpriced. We were looking at that and we were like, I can pay that much and save this much of his time. And we try to price his time and try to price my time on all the things we do. And like, if Ty's going to budget two hours on a thing, what's that worth? So it's not worth the enterprise. Hey, Joseph's got a budget. Three hours to the thing. What's that worth to Enterprise? And we looked at the Bloomberg.
turns.zh: 它是被低估的。我们当时算了算，然后想：我可以付那么多钱，同时省下他那么多时间。我们试着给他所有的工作定价，也试着给我的时间定价。比如说，如果 Tice 打算在一件事上花两个小时，那值多少钱？对企业来说值不值。嘿，Joseph 有预算：在这件事上花三个小时。那对企业来说值多少钱？然后我们看了看彭博的价格。

turns.en: Wait, so you say you have a low return on brain damage. A little bit of conflict there. But you carefully calculate the value of your time. Yeah. And so people call you up with weird trades and you're like, nope, not worth it to think about it. That's not true. You think about it.
turns.zh: 等等，你不是说你有很低的‘脑损伤回报率’吗？这里有点自相矛盾。但你会仔细计算自己时间的价值。——是的。——所以别人打电话来跟你说古怪的交易，你就说：不，不值得我去想。——那不是真的。你会去想。

turns.en: Yeah, that's fun. That's the fun part. Sit in the hot tub, sit on the roof, think about the fun stuff.
turns.zh: 是啊，那是好玩的。那才是好玩的部分。坐在按摩浴缸里，坐在屋顶上，想那些有意思的事。

turns.en: That's good. So your time for doing administrative or number crunching work is highly valuable, but your time for thinking about weird trades is?
turns.zh: 这挺好。所以你用来做行政或者算数字的时间非常有价值，但你用来琢磨古怪交易的时间就不值钱？

turns.en: But that's where the money came from. So I'd rather just sit around and think about things. It's been interesting.
turns.zh: 可钱就是从那儿来的。所以我宁愿就坐在那儿想事情。这一直很有意思。

turns.en: It's a good life. I also like to sit around and think about weird dreads, but it's a different economic model.
turns.zh: 这是好日子。我也喜欢坐在那儿琢磨古怪的交易，但那是另一种经济模式。

turns.en: It doesn't have to be, man. Come do fun stuff.
turns.zh: 不一定非得这样，哥们儿。来一起做点好玩的事。

turns.en: I have fun now. You do.
turns.zh: 我现在就很好玩。——你确实是。

turns.en: You have the most fun of anyone I know.
turns.zh: 你是我认识的人里玩得最开心的。

turns.en: Is that true? Absolutely.
turns.zh: 真的吗？——绝对真的。

turns.en: You look at a bunch of different fascinating things. You get to pick what fascinates you. Does someone feed you the things to do you don't think?
turns.zh: 你能研究一堆不同的、迷人的东西。你可以自己挑什么让你着迷。你觉得是有人在给你派活儿吗？

turns.en: No, I mean.
turns.zh: 不是，我是说……

turns.en: top down within Bloomberg. You seem to do the things that fascinate you. And the things you write fascinate me. It fascinates everybody. That's a good thing. It's a good show. I don't mean to toot your horn. It's a good show.
turns.zh: ……彭博内部自上而下地派。你看起来做的都是让你自己着迷的事。而你写的东西让我着迷，让所有人都着迷。这是件好事。这是个好节目。我不是要给你吹喇叭，但这是个好节目。

turns.en: I think we're going to end it there. Let's end it. Tyce Brown, thanks for coming on to the Money Stuff Podcast.
turns.zh: 我觉得我们就聊到这儿吧。就这样结束。Tice Brown，谢谢你来上《Money Stuff》播客。

turns.en: Thank you for having me, Matt. It's been an honor.
turns.zh: 谢谢你请我来，Matt。这是我的荣幸。

turns.en: Do you want to, like, you don't have any socials. You don't care. No one needs to contact you.
turns.zh: 你要不要……你根本没有社交媒体账号。你不在乎。也没人需要联系你。

turns.en: I'm just a guy. Please don't contact me.
turns.zh: 我就是个普通人。请不要联系我。
